utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, this is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'd like to deal with a few preliminary matters. For the first one, we have to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I hereby publicly announce that the Chamber has just delivered in private session its decision granting the Defence motion for protective measures for Witness GRM246. A few other matters. The first, a request for extension of time. On the 8th of September, 2014, the Defence requested an extension of time to file its notices pursuant to Rule 94 bis for six proposed expert witnesses who the Prosecution seeks to call as part of its anticipated reopening of its case. The Defence requested a deadline to be set to 60 days after the Chamber has decided on the Prosecution's reopening motion. The Prosecution did not object to this. The Chamber considers that it would not be efficient to require the Defence to state its position before a decision on the reopening motion is made. The extension request is therefore granted. The next item deals with Witness Drinic. On the 15th of September, 2014, the Defence filed a Rule 92 ter motion for Witness Predrag Drinic. This witness is not on the Defence's Rule 65 ter witness list and, in fact, a request to add him to the list was denied by the Chamber on the 12th of August, 2014. Under these circumstances, the Chamber denies the Rule 92 ter motion for Witness Drinic. The Chamber advises the Defence to reread the Chamber's decision of the 12th of August of this year. I now move to the 92 ter motion in relation to Desimir Sarenac and especially the exhibits associated with it. The Defence has tendered 25 associated exhibits for Witness Desimir Sarenac. The Chamber reminds the parties that it will not accept to be flooded with associated exhibits. The Chamber expects the Defence to not consider it standard practice to tender a large number of associated exhibits with each witness. This includes the length as well as the number of tendered exhibits. The Chamber recalls that it prefers that documents are tendered during the witness's examination in court which allows the witness to explain and comment on them. We will deal with the matter when the witness is called and when the Defence has made up its mind as to how to deal with the associated exhibits. Then we have to turn into closed session for the witness to enter the courtroom in view of the face distortion. We move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness GRM246, because that's how we will call you, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday when you appeared in court. You will first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You will find Mr. Ivetic to your left, and as I told you yesterday, Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Mladic Defence team. You may proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could first ask that you take a look at 1D03119 which should not be broadcast. Sir, this is a pseudonym sheet, and could you please tell us if your name and birth date are accurately reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could admit this under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D3119 receives number D644, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D644 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to call up but also not broadcast the document 1D04216. And if we can turn to the last page in the Serbian original.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the signature that is reflected herein, do you recognise whose signature it is?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And after signing the same on the date indicated, did you have occasion to review it in Serbian to correct any errors during your proofing session with me the other day?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we did that and we corrected some errors.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak louder. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're invited to raise your voice, to speak a bit louder so that the interpreters can hear you. Perhaps you could come a bit closer to the microphone as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we reviewed that and we corrected the errors that we noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, apart from these corrections that we have just gone through, do you stand behind the material written in this statement as being factually accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you today questions on the same topics as contained in this statement, would your answers to those questions be in substance the same?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And since today you are under the solemn declaration to tell the truth, does that mean that those answers as contained in this written statement are truthful in nature?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this document under seal as the next Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would ask that it just remain MFI'd pending the resolution of associated exhibits since there are a lot of them and the statement's based on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was going to deal with associated exhibits at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, fine, but meanwhile we MFI the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number under which it would be MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4216 receives number D646, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D646 is marked for identification under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just know what exhibits are being tendered for the purposes of cross-examination at some point in time in -- before the end of the witness altogether, just so I can plan my examination accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, is the Defence in a position to provide a short list of documents that will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe we provided a list. I believe there are 45 exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think there was also a request to reduce the number. Is there any reduced list?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is no reduced list, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir -- I would like to again call up the document we just dealt with, D646, MFI'd under seal. It should not be public -- it should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the first page, in the first point, you discuss six documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I want to call up the last one from that list, but again we should not broadcast it. And in our case, its 65 ter number is 1D04225. I'd like to first look at the -- first look at the last page of the document in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just before we return to open session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would just note the placement of the screens and the gallery, maybe with some of the names in the documents just to be conscientious about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it that this has been verified. Could the usher just check whether all the screens are either switched off or in such positions that they cannot be observed from the public gallery. Please proceed meanwhile, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document purports to be issued in your name but signed by another person. Can you confirm for us if this person was authorised to sign on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes. In my absence, most often it would be the deputy or one of the assistants who would sign this. In this case it was the deputy and he was authorised to sign the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you stand behind the contents of such a document signed by the deputy?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now if we can stay on this page in the Serbian and in the English, the last paragraph is what I'd like to ask you about. Here it is said that: "Muslims have snipers in the National Museum," albeit in the English it is mistranslated as "sharpshooter," and "that these persons fire upon not only Grbavica but also the area around the railway station to seek to attribute their effects to the Serb army." First of all, who controlled the area around the railway station? Was it the Army of BiH or the VRS?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Well, the area of the railway station was covered by the BiH army and it was in the centre of their territory. So their control was in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, who were the Muslim snipers shooting at with the aim to attribute it to the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Well, in this case, they could only fire at the Muslim population or, rather, the citizens who were in that area, regardless of whether they were Muslims, Croats or Serbs. The intention was to create panic. And this would happen most often when something important would be happening in Sarajevo, a session attended by the international community or some other important events when the TV crews were there and then they would use this propaganda to a maximum: Here they go again, the Chetniks, they're firing, in order to create as much commotion as possible and to create the worst possible picture of the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in this document, you even name one of the female snipers here. How reliable did you consider this information to be?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Well, all the information in this document have been marked to the extent of their reliability. In this case, the information says that it was 99 per cent accurate. That was corroborated from various sources, whether by live persons or otherwise. Anyway, this was credible and verified information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we could return to the first page of the document and again still not broadcast the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It would appear that this document lists several other official notes all dated from April 1993. Does that comport with your recollection that multiple reports were prepared on the same topics as contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Well, yes, the general practice was that after multiple communications containing information, whether it be official notes or other forms of communication, an overall information would be compiled pertaining to a certain date or a certain event. Here, this describes the current military situation in the area of Sarajevo, in the parts under Muslim control. That is what the information says, that it's based on the information intelligence from the National Security Service obtained with regard to the Muslim-controlled areas of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence would tender this document under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D4225 receives number D647, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D647 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, sir -- I'd like to ask you, sir, about something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have D645 under seal but not broadcast. And if we could go to page 3 in the English and I believe it should be 3 in the B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Here you talk about the incident at Markale being staged and you give us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 9, I apologise. Paragraph 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You talk about the Markale incident being staged and you identify two sources. Since we're in open session, I do not want to identify the sources, but I want to ask you, first of all, if you recall which of the Markale incidents this is in reference to?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: This is in reference to the Markale when a shell allegedly fell and killed over 70 citizens and wounded more than 80, if we are not wrong about the figures provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the year of the incident in question?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: I think it was 1993. I'm not quite sure. I cannot remember exactly. If we go back now to the date when the statement was written down, we might establish other facts accurately as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way, do you recall if there was more than one Markale incident of this nature?

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were more than one incident, but I think in this particular case, it relates to the event that was devastating for a large number of citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've been reminded that we did not do a summary of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at the same time there's a risk that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- somewhere the clues for identifying the witness would pop up and that's perhaps under the present circumstances better to avoid.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be my position as well, Your Honour. Thank you, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, thank you for your answers to my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That concludes the direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you one brief question in relation to a matter which was raised by Mr. Ivetic about the Markale incident being staged. A reference is made to refrigerated corpses. Did you, apart from hearing this from someone, did you ever find any other evidence apart from it being told to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look, mainly many interviews were conducted with live persons and also written statements were provided to that effect. However, here, the focus is only one source. There were many people who managed to cross over, and there were pictures and footage on TV immediately after the landing of the shell which shows an expert for counter-terrorist protection which means that that was a person who was quite capable of making a fake explosive device and he's seen entering buildings. So if I could see that footage again, I could tell you who the expert was in this particular area. Secondly, what indicated that it was a staged event was that there were literally no broken stalls. There was no blood. One could only hear crying and wails, one could not see dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. First of all, I have some concern - I'm now addressing the parties - that a person entering a building remind me very much of what is commonly known in this courtroom as Markale 2 rather than as Markale 1, but I may be mistaken. So if that's the case, then the witness might mix up at this moment videos he has seen on one and on the other Markale market incident. Witness, you have heard what I said, that when you saw a video of a person entering a building, the Chamber has seen such a video but it was not related to the Markale incident you are describing. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, at this moment, I cannot remember exactly which incident it was. I'm talking about the incident when a large number of citizens were killed or at least that's what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll continue there, then, about the stalls and a large number of -- I think you mentioned 60 or about 60. I asked you whether you ever found any evidence about refrigerated corpses, apart from it once being told to you. That was my question. I didn't ask you to give your general opinion about what happened on that market.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there was no other evidence and we did not have an expert for that. But this did not come from one source alone. It came from many sources, from people who crossed over, from people who were working for the international community, et cetera. However, there is no other proof other than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If there are more sources for specific details of that, Mr. Ivetic, I take it that the Defence would certainly further explore that item. You will now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. You find Mr. Weber to your right. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Weber. I leave it to you whether you want to turn into private session at this moment or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was just going to greet the witness and then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: GRM246
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. So if nothing special happens, one more session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I'm actually going to try to -- a lot of the documents I think I can maybe just show to him, have him confirm information, and then move on quickly, if that's okay with Your Honours, to expedite --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are presenting the evidence, Mr. Weber. As long as you stay within the Rules, we do not provide you with specific instructions or suggestions. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Friday, the 19th of September, 2014, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of September, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.20 p.m.,
